title: Introducing the NS 200 Locomotive Series
body_markdown:
*Three commemorative locomotives honor the people, predecessor railroads, and progress that have shaped Norfolk Southern*


To commemorate[Norfolk Southern’s 200th anniversary](https://www.norfolksouthern.com/en/newsroom/news-releases/norfolk-southern-celebrates-200-years-of-railroading--unveils-anniversary-campaign-and-commemorative-locomotives) , the NS 200 Locomotive Series – three specially designed locomotives – will celebrate the people, predecessor railroads, and progress that have shaped Norfolk Southern.


Together, the series honors the generations who built our railroad, the railroaders moving it forward today, and those who will carry our legacy into the future.


**Top Takeaways**


- Three specially designed locomotives – No. 4980, No. 4981, and No. 4982 – commemorate Norfolk Southern’s 200th anniversary.
- Each unit tells part of the story: The 1827 honors two centuries of hard work, The 200 honors our predecessor railroads, and The Thoroughbred honors generations of railroaders.
- Gold, a traditional bicentennial color, joins Norfolk Southern’s iconic black and white scheme on each locomotive.


**No. 4980 – The 1827**


The 1827 is a rolling tribute to two centuries of hard work and a genuine source of pride for everyone who sees it and every crew who runs it.


**No. 4981 – The 200**


The 200 is a tribute to our predecessors. By bringing their logos together beneath the Norfolk Southern banner, the design honors the many railroads that came before us and celebrates how far we’ve come. It is a visual reminder that our heritage is the foundation for the railroad we continue to build today.


**No. 4982 – The Thoroughbred**


The Thoroughbred is a tribute to our people. Rendered as our iconic symbol in a bold black silhouette, the design conveys honor and pride. It is a reminder that Norfolk Southern’s strength has always come from the people who move us forward.


**Built by railroaders, marked by gold**


Our skilled railroaders at Juniata Locomotive Shop in Altoona, Pennsylvania, will craft each unit, which are all freshly built DC-to-AC locomotives. Gold, a traditional bicentennial color, is added to Norfolk Southern's iconic black and white paint scheme to mark the significance of this historic milestone.


**Join us at the Norfolk Southern Heritage Days**


Beginning in Spring 2027, NS will celebrate with our team and communities across the network on the[Norfolk Southern Heritage Days tour](https://norfolksouthern.com/200Years) . These events will give employees, customers, and the public a chance to explore our railroad’s history and see the anniversary locomotives up close.


Each stop will be hosted in a place that has played a significant role in railroading history, celebrating the generations of people and defining moments that have shaped Norfolk Southern’s story.


Event locations and additional details will be announced in the coming weeks!
